name: Dread-Enormous
geological_features: Hypercane storm systems exceeding planetary diameters of terrestrial worlds
Liquid metallic hydrogen ocean beneath the gas envelope
Radiation belts capable of sterilizing unshielded vessels
specific_features: Gravitational influence disrupts navigation systems within three AU
A debris field of destroyed ships in decaying orbit
description: Dread-Enormous pushes the definition of gas giant to its theoretical limits, a world so massive it nearly achieved stellar ignition during its formation. At one hundred and forty-eight thousand kilometers in diameter, its gravitational influence warps the orbits of everything within three astronomical units, and its radiation belts can sterilize an unshielded vessel in minutes.

The toxic atmosphere churns with hypercane storms of planet-swallowing scale, their winds exceeding three thousand kilometers per hour in the upper layers. The magnetic field generated by the liquid metallic hydrogen ocean beneath the gas envelope is powerful enough to induce hallucinations in crew members through electromagnetic interference with neural tissue.

A debris field of destroyed ships orbits in a decaying ring around the planet, testament to vessels that ventured too close and were torn apart by tidal forces or fried by radiation. The oldest wreckage dates back centuries, the newest is less than a year old, and the pattern shows no sign of ending as long as the planet's resources remain tempting.

The antimatter naturally produced in the planet's radiation belts represents the greatest energy resource in the sector, enough to power a civilization for millennia. But Dread-Enormous defends its bounty with the implacable physics of mass and energy, and every ton of fuel extracted has cost lives and ships in a ratio that accountants call unsustainable and captains call the price of necessity.
